elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The new paragraph (d) contains a direct IP claim limb, but it is placed after Section 14.2(a), under Sanofi's indemnity to RevMed. It therefore operates in the wrong direction. Section 14.1's reference to cases “(a) through (d)” does not create or incorporate a substantive paragraph (d) into RevMed's indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 covers material breaches of contractual representations, warranties, and obligations, but does not expressly cover RevMed's breach of law. No applicable legal-compliance obligation is shown.

elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach indemnity trigger appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 requires RevMed to indemnify and defend Sanofi and its Affiliates against Third Party Claims arising from RevMed Indemnitees' negligence; this encompasses gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must defend and indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 expressly covers Third Party Claims arising from the willful misconduct of RevMed Indemnitees and provides indemnification and defense for Sanofi and its Affiliates.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No notice procedure is included in the rendered language.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defense of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No defense-control provision is included in the rendered language.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide reasonable cooperation in defending a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation is included in the rendered language.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2(a) does not identify Customer-provided content as an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The shown portion of Section 14.2 does not provide an express indemnity trigger for Sanofi's breach of law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must contain no triggers other than Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2(a) broadly requires Sanofi to indemnify for claims arising from research, development, manufacture, or commercialization of products, which exceeds the permitted Customer indemnity scope. The misplaced paragraph (d) further expands Sanofi's indemnity to IP claims.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that Vendor's services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Although paragraph (d) states a direct IP claim trigger, its placement under Section 14.2 makes Sanofi the indemnifying party and RevMed the beneficiary. RevMed therefore does not provide the required Vendor IP indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity may exclude claims caused by Customer's unauthorized modifications to the covered services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d)(i) contains a Sanofi-modification exclusion, but it qualifies the misplaced Sanofi-to-RevMed indemnity rather than a Vendor IP indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity may exclude claims caused by combining the covered services or deliverables with items not provided or specified by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d)(ii) contains a combination exclusion, but it qualifies the misplaced Sanofi-to-RevMed indemnity rather than a Vendor IP indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for claims caused by compliance with Sanofi-provided specifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have the remedy of procuring Customer's continued right to use the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No procurement-of-rights remedy is included.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have the remedy of modifying the affected services or deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No non-infringing modification remedy is included.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have the remedy of replacing the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy is included.

elements.element: If the other infringement remedies are unavailable, Vendor must refund the applicable fees for the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy is included.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no three-times-annual-fees super-cap or other stated cap specifically applicable to Vendor's IP indemnity.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve either position. Its central defect is structural: Section 14.1 is changed to reference cases “(a) through (d),” but no substantive paragraph (d) is placed within Section 14.1. Instead, paragraph (d) follows Section 14.2(a), whose introductory language makes Sanofi the indemnitor and RevMed the indemnitee. The addition therefore creates a Customer-to-Vendor IP indemnity—the opposite of the intended Vendor-to-Customer protection. It also omits the preferred law, data-breach, procedure, and limited Customer-indemnity requirements, as well as the fallback specification exclusion, infringement remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap. The reversed indemnity direction introduces a material contradiction and expands Customer's liability.
